newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat stake in New Holland 69 pct after IPO. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Fiat stake in New Holland 69 pct after IPO. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Fiat SpA's said its stake in New Holland NV could be reduced to 69 percent after New Holland's Initial Public Offering later this month.
New Holland NV said in a registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it planned to sell up to 53,475,000 common shares or $1.23 billion.
Fiat said in a statement released in London and made available in Milan that the IPO was expected to take place towards the end of October.

New Holland said the total global offering was of 46.5 million shares. (Corrects to clarify that total offer size is 46.5 million shares and deletes reference to U.S.) The underwriters have been granted an over-allotment option of up to 6,975,000 additional shares.
The shares are being offered by New Holland's parent company New Holland Holding NV which is entirely controlled by Fiat SpA.
Fiat said that after the global offering New Holland Holding NV would own about 69 percent of the 149 million ordinary shares of New Holland in circulation if the green shoe option was not exercised.
Joint global coordinators for the global offering will be Mediobanca and Goldman Sachs International.
For the public offering in the U.S., Goldman Sachs & Co is lead manager. Co-lead managers are Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, Merrill Lynch & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc.

For the international offering to institutional investors outside the U.S. and Italy, lead managers are Mediobanca and Goldman Sachs International. Co-leads are Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Paribas and SBC Warburg.
For the offer to professional investors in Italy, Mediobanca is the lead manager, with Banca Commerciale Italiana, Banca di Roma and Credito Italiano as co-lead managers.

New Holland was formed in May 1991 when Fiat SpA acquired Ford New Holland Inc, merging its commercial activities with those of Fiat Geotech. New Holland is a world leader in the design, construction, marketing and distribution of agricultural equipment.
